Hidasi–Karatzoglou’s BPR-max is L = −log(Σⱼ wⱼ σ(r₊−rⱼ)) + λΣⱼ wⱼrⱼ², where wⱼ = exp(rⱼ)/Σₖexp(rₖ), normalized over negative positions. The logarithm surrounds the weighted sum of sigmoid probabilities; this differs from a weighted sum of pairwise log-losses. The second term penalizes negative output scores, distinct from parameter weight decay. [Paper, Eq. 16](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf)

The original official implementation adds 1e−24 inside the logarithm and differentiates through the softmax weights in both terms; detaching weights changes the objective’s gradient. Negative sampling is with replacement, and duplicates remain separate score columns, so multiplicity affects their total softmax mass. Only each row’s designated positive diagonal position is excluded: another column containing the same item ID is still treated as negative. Deduplication or masking all target-ID collisions therefore changes this implementation’s behavior. [Official loss, sampler and training code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/master/gru4rec.py)

Scores are outputs after the selected final activation, used consistently in score differences, negative softmax weights and quadratic regularization. BPR-max supports linear, ReLU, tanh, leaky-ReLU, ELU and SELU outputs; the author commonly prefers ELU with α=0.5 or 1. The negative-weight softmax is internal to the loss, distinct from a softmax output activation. Activation, sampling, duplicate handling and λ should be reported alongside any claimed BPR-max improvement. [Official activation guidance](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/blob/master/README.md)
